page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance from the legacy n1 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting Hyper-Threading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of approximately 0.9 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the instance delivers modest processing capabilities. In single-core and multi-core CPU tests via stress-ng, performance falls within the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the poor and weak categories respectively. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in specific workloads, such as Geekbench ray tracing and Passmark CPU scores, which sit in the middle 50%. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations also achieve average tier results, whereas small-block cached reads are weak.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-8 is its highly constrained memory allocation relative to its compute cores, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense allocation of dedicated vCPUs within an older hardware class, making it a viable option for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. Suitable workloads include parallelizable CPU tasks, basic software compilation, ray tracing, and lightweight text or image processing pipelines that fit comfortably within the 7.0 GB memory limit.
